analysis:
Examined SandboxInstaller.swift and SandboxSetupCommand.swift. The PR adds a repeatable `--disk` option for work disks (external APFS drives). Setup checks each drive, can offer `sudo diskutil enableOwnership`, and passes the absolute paths to the downloaded install.sh.

SandboxInstaller.swift:
- `sizingArguments` (line 133-138) appends `["--disk", path]` pairs to an argv array.
- The installer runs via `SandboxChildProcess.run(/bin/sh, [installer.path] + args)`, not through a shell string. Owner-supplied or drive-derived paths therefore cannot inject shell syntax at this boundary.
- `supportsDisks` is a substring match on the downloaded script text, the same trust model as `supportsPlan` and `supportsJSONProgress`. It is a compatibility gate, not a security control.
- Download validation is unchanged: HTTPS only, HTTPS-only redirects, 1 MiB cap, shebang check.

SandboxSetupCommand.swift:
- `withInstaller` now refuses `--disk` for an installer that does not name it. This prevents passing unknown arguments to older installers and fails before anything changes.
- `ownershipToTurnOn` and `turnOnOwnership` run `enableOwnership(mount)` only when all of these hold: not `--yes`, a TTY is present, the single problem is ownershipOff, and the owner confirms at a prompt. This is an owner-initiated privileged action with explicit consent, and it is never run under `--yes`.
- The failure path in `requestAddonPlan` prints the last 5 stderr lines from the installer when disks are given. Those lines come from an installer that already runs as the owner under T-061, so this adds no new trust.
- `chooseWorkDisk` runs only on the fresh path, at a prompt, for an installer that names `--disk`.

T-061 and TB-013 are not weakened. The installer's own publisher-signature and digest verification remains the control, and no new network surface was added.

Not supplied, so integration questions remain:
- `SandboxWorkDisk.{absolutePath, volume, candidates, check, problem, enableOwnership}`: how the mount point is passed to `sudo diskutil` (argv vs shell), whether the volume name is sanitized before terminal printing, and whether symlink or path traversal is normalized.
- Whether the add-on or installer treats work-disk paths safely.
- Whether a work-disk-held VM image or job data protection posture is covered in TB-013.

No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence.
